title: Duties to relatives
intro: Keeping family ties is a duty Allah commanded.

learn.html: One of the duties Allah commanded is our duty to our relatives. Sadly, many Muslims don’t know that these duties are commanded by Allah.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah commands justice, doing good and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, evil and oppression. He advises you so that you take heed. <small>(Qur’an, An-Nahl 16:90)</small>

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “By the One who sent me with the truth, Allah will not accept sadaqah, nor look on the Day of Judgement at a man who has relatives in need of his help and does not help them.” (Tabarani)

items: love them for the sake of Allah
look after them and visit them regularly
help them as much as we can
make peace between relatives who have fallen out
visit even those who don’t visit back
respect relatives even if they are not Muslims
we bring joy to our relatives’ hearts
Allah rewards us with a longer life
we come closer to Jannah and further from Jahannam

practice.title: Keeping family ties
practice.prompt: Tap everything that keeps family ties, then tap Check.

options.text: Calling an aunt who is ill
Making peace between cousins who fell out
Visiting a relative who never visits back
Refusing to talk to an uncle after an argument
options.why: We make peace and keep family ties.

questions.q: What does keeping family ties bring, according to the hadiths?
options: A longer life and more provision

questions.q: Must we respect relatives who are not Muslims?

practice.title: Questions
prompts: 💭 Why do you sometimes feel lonely? Does visiting relatives help?
🤝 How can visiting relatives help a person feel better?
